battle.name: 孫華起義
battle.brief: 大業十二年冬，隋泗州蕭縣裨將孫華聚眾起事，眾至數萬，一度攻陷郡縣，隋廷遣軍討平。卡面的埃及月牙劍屬公元前十五世紀的青銅短兵，與隋軍制式環首直刀形制全然不同，並不在此役現場；起義眾所恃為竹木矛叉柴刀，官軍則以環首刀、弓矢、明光鎧與攻城器械應戰。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 這場起義是隋大業十二年（616年）冬在淮北泗州蕭縣爆發的一次地方叛亂，屬隋末民變浪潮的前段。起義方並非一個國家或王朝，而是由蕭縣一帶鄉里百姓、逃兵、逃戶與被裁汰的鄉兵拼湊而成的武裝集團，首領孫華原為隋軍的基層裨將。官軍一方是隋朝中央在泗州、汴州一線的州郡兵鎮：泗州刺史、郡丞與縣令所領的郡兵是最早投入的骨幹，鄰近州郡亦奉詔出兵會剿，隋煬帝楊廣自江都巡幸途中聞變，下令限期平定，未有大軍西進。起義爆發時，隋朝在名義上仍控制長江以北至遼東的廣大區域，州縣衙署、糧倉、漕運線與驛傳系統俱在運作，因此這不是國家之間的戰爭，而是帝國內部的平叛作戰。戰區位於汴水至淮水一線的交通要衝，泗州蕭縣控扼汴泗運河北段與鄉里糧倉，叛軍一旦據此，官軍的漕運與東都洛陽的糧道即受牽動；此役同時是一場補給線與內部秩序的爭奪。
countriesEn: This uprising was a local revolt that broke out in the winter of the twelfth year of the Daye era (616) at Xiao county in Si prefecture on the northern bank of the Huai river, in the opening phase of the wave of popular risings that shook the late Sui. The rebel side was not a state or a dynasty but an armed mass assembled in the villages around Xiao county out of local peasants, deserters, runaway households and dismissed local militia; its leader, Sun Hua, had been a junior bingjiang officer of the Sui army. On the government side stood the prefectural and commandery troops of the Sui centre along the line of Si prefecture and Bian prefecture: the commandery soldiers under the prefect, the deputy prefect and the county magistrate of Si were the first troops committed, neighbouring prefectures were ordered to send contingents, and Emperor Yang of Sui, then touring Jiangdu by imperial boat, ordered the matter closed by a set date without moving the main army west. When the revolt broke out the Sui still nominally held everything from the Yangtze north to Liaodong, with the offices of the prefectures and counties, the granaries, the canal traffic and the courier relay all still working, so this was not a war between states but a pacification operation inside the empire. The theatre lies on the traffic artery of the Bian and Huai waterways: Xiao county in Si prefecture commanded the northern stretch of the Bian-Si canal and the village granaries, and once the rebels held it the grain route to the eastern capital Luoyang was put at risk. For that reason the campaign was at the same time a struggle over a supply line and over internal order.
people: 核心人物是起義首領孫華。他是隋軍在泗州一帶的裨將，屬隋代軍制中基層的什將、隊正之屬，品秩低微，卻熟悉部伍編制與操練之法，這一出身使他在起義之初能迅速聚起一支粗具建制的隊伍。史籍對孫華的記載止於數語：其人為蕭人，官裨將，於大業十二年冬聚眾反，先據本縣，再掠鄰近州縣，旋為官軍所平，首領被誅，餘眾潰散。除此之外可考的相關人物，多從官軍一端看這場衝突。隋煬帝楊廣此時在位第十二年，正以龍舟巡幸江都，聞訊後只令地方限期討平；地方刺史、郡丞與縣令奉詔募兵討賊，郡兵成為平叛主力。同期在中原各地平叛的名將張須陀，於大業十一年至十三年間在山東、河北一線屢破張金吾、麴士陸等部，可作官軍作戰方式之參照；而此前已有大業七年山東王薄起義、大業九年黎陽楊玄感之役、大業十一年山東張金吾之亂，說明孫華並非孤例，而是隋末亂序的一環。
peopleEn: The central figure is Sun Hua, the leader of the rising. He was a bingjiang, a low-ranking officer of the Sui military system, of the kind of platoon and section leader who manned the ranks; the grade was minor but the drill was real, and it was this background that let him raise a body with an improvised order of battle within days of the outbreak. The records about Sun Hua himself amount to a few lines: a man of Xiao county, a bingjiang by appointment, who rose in arms in the winter of the twelfth year of Daye, first seizing his own county and then raiding the neighbouring prefectures and counties, only to be crushed by the government troops, with the leaders executed and the rest scattered. Beyond him, the people who can be documented for this conflict are mostly those on the government side. Emperor Yang of Sui, in the twelfth year of his reign, was touring Jiangdu with the imperial flotilla; on hearing of the revolt he ordered the local authorities to close the matter by a set date and did not move the main army west. The prefect, deputy prefect and magistrates of the prefectures and counties were ordered to raise troops, and the commandery militia became the backbone of the suppression. The famous Sui commander Zhang Xutuo, who repeatedly broke Zhang Jinwu and Qu Shilu in the Shandong and Hebei area between the eleventh and thirteenth years of Daye, provides a useful reference for how the government fought such risings. Earlier risings by Wang Bo in Shandong in the seventh year of Daye, by Yang Xuangan at Liyang in the ninth and by Zhang Jinwu in Shandong in the eleventh had already shown that Sun Hua was no isolated case but one link in a chain of disorder.
kits: 卡面兵器是埃及月牙劍（Khopesh），約公元前十五世紀的青銅短兵，單刃外彎，刃形與劍脊構成月牙狀，設計上使砍擊入肉後不需像直刃刀那樣拔出再割。器形起源於埃及與西亞一帶，現存者多見於歐洲博物館的收藏，故在兵種與工藝譜系上屬青銅時代的埃及—西亞系統，而非東方的鐵器兵器。此役現場並無月牙劍：隋軍的標準佩刀是環首直刀，刀身平直無弧，柄首成環，作單手劈刺之用，與月牙劍不拔刀而割的用法恰成對照；起義眾所用則多為鄉里可就地取材的竹木長矛、木叉、柴刀與短刀，配以粗製皮盾與弓箭，缺甲胄，攻城倚靠雲梯、撞車等常備器械。就戰役功能而言，月牙劍象徵的是早期重刃冷兵器這一技術世代，它比隋刀早出約二千一百一十六年，以青銅硬度與外彎刃勢換取斬擊威力；而隋戰場上的真實兵器已換成兩千餘年演進後的環首直刀、鐵矛與弓弩，兩者分屬完全不同的技術脈絡，月牙劍只能作為對照的標尺，而非此役的實戰裝備。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Egyptian khopesh, a short bronze sword of about the fifteenth century BC, single-edged and curved outward, its blade and spine forming a crescent, and designed so that once it has entered the target it does not have to be pulled back and sawed the way a straight-edged blade does. The type originated in Egypt and western Asia, and the surviving examples are mostly held in European museum collections, so in typological and metallurgical terms it belongs to the bronze-age Egyptian and Levantine system rather than to the iron weaponry of the Far East. No khopesh was present on the field of this campaign. The standard sidearm of the Sui army was the ring-pommel straight sabre, with a flat blade of no curvature and a ring at the end of the hilt, used one-handed for cutting and thrusting, and that is the exact opposite of the khopesh, which never needs to be drawn back. The rebels, for their part, used whatever their villages could provide: bamboo and wooden spears, wooden forks, woodcutting blades and short knives, with coarse hide shields and plain bows, and little or no armour. They took towns with gates, breaches in the rampart and insiders rather than heavy siege equipment, while the Sui side brought to the task the battering ram, the siege ladder and fire, the standard siege kit of the time. As for the khopesh in the context of this war, it stands for the earlier generation of heavy-edged cold weapons: it predates the Sui sabre by roughly two thousand one hundred and sixteen years and trades on the hardness of bronze and the leverage of an outward curve, while the actual blades on the Sui battlefield had been replaced, after more than two millennia of development, by ring-pommel straight sabres, iron spears and crossbows. The two belong to entirely different technical lineages, and the khopesh can only serve as a comparative marker, not as equipment that fought at Xiao.
tactics: 起義方的作法，是先以蕭縣城與周邊鄉里為依託，於市集、渡口一帶聚眾，再循泗水、汴水的水陸便路向鄰近州縣分進；鄉里之間塘堰、柳林與草澤可資遮蔽，人數一多即能遮斷縣道，使官軍的偵騎難以確知其主力所在，故《隋書》與《資治通鑑》都只記眾至數萬，而其分佈始終不明。攻城時，叛軍倚賴城門、城牆缺口與內應，而非大型攻城器械；破城之後則取糧倉、官署與武庫之器，把郡縣的儲糧與甲兵轉為自用，這正是隋代州縣小吏與鄉兵難以抵禦的弱點。官軍方面，隋廷最初不欲投入主力，只令泗州刺史、郡丞與鄰州出郡兵會剿，方針以速定為主：一是集中兵力直撲叛軍集結之處，二是分兵斷絕其糧秣與往來商旅，三是在平定後收編散眾、捕拿首領。整個作戰受制於兩點：一是隋代郡兵本身規模有限，多為農隙應募的鄉兵，戰力遠不及鎮守京城的宿衛禁軍；二是蕭縣距東都洛陽約八百里，距汴州五百餘里，距離意味著糧秣須靠沿途州縣就地輸送，一旦運道被擾，平叛的成本立刻上升。
tacticsEn: The rebels based themselves on the county seat of Xiao and the surrounding villages, gathering at markets and river crossings, and then pushed out towards the neighbouring prefectures and counties along the convenient water and land routes of the Si and Bian rivers. The country between them was full of ponds, dykes, willow scrub and marshes that gave cover, and once their numbers grew they could cut the county roads, so imperial scouts could never pin down where the main body actually stood. That is why both the Suishu and the Zizhi Tongjian record only that their numbers reached tens of thousands, while their distribution remained unknown. In taking towns they relied on gates, gaps in the walls and insiders rather than heavy siege equipment, and once a city fell they took the granaries, the government offices and the armoury, converting the stores of the commandery into their own supplies; this was the weakness that small Sui officials and local militia could not absorb. On the government side the court did not wish to commit the main army: the prefect of Si, the deputy prefect and the neighbouring prefectures were ordered to send commandery troops, and the guiding principle was speed. Three measures were combined: concentrate the force against the place where the rebels had massed, detach troops to cut their grain and to stop the merchants and travellers who might feed them, and after the rising was broken, take in the scattered men and seize the leaders. The whole operation was held down by two constraints. First, the Sui commandery militia was small in numbers and poorly trained, recruited as it was from peasants in the slack farming season, and it was no match for the palace guards of the capital. Second, Xiao county lies about eight hundred li from the eastern capital Luoyang and more than five hundred li from Bian prefecture; those distances mean the grain must be carried by the prefectures along the route, and the moment the line of supply is disturbed the cost of the pacification rises at once.
data: 可核的數字並不多，且多屬體量與背景，非本役雙方的細帳。《隋書·食貨志》記開皇末年隋朝有戶約八百九十萬、口約四千四百六十萬；《隋書·地理志》記隋疆域東西九千五百里、南北一萬六千九百一十八里，說明這場起義發生在一個仍具可觀徵發能力的帝國腹地，州縣的兵糧來源在紙面上依然充裕。但徵發本身正在耗損這份能力：大業七年第一次征高句麗時，隋廷集兵百十三萬、號稱二百萬，糧秣盡於遼東，士卒死亡者以十數萬計，其後大業八年、九年、十一年又三度再征。同期江淮、江南連年水旱，倉廩不繼，逃戶與流民成為起義最直接的人力來源。就本役而言，史料可用的只有眾至數萬一語與先陷郡縣的次序記載，無從核出叛軍與官軍的實數；起事在大業十二年冬爆發，至大業十三年初已平定，前後不過二、三個月，戰役本身的時間跨度遠短於它在隋末亂局中所代表的意義。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are few, and most of them describe scale and background rather than the accounts of the two sides in this campaign. The Suishu's Treatise on Economics records that in the closing years of the Kaihuang era the Sui had some 8.9 million households and about 44.6 million people, and the Treatise on Geography gives the extent of the empire as 9,500 li from east to west and 16,918 li from north to south; this uprising therefore broke out in the interior of an empire that still possessed a considerable capacity to raise men, and on paper the prefectures and counties still had ample sources of soldiers and grain. Yet the levies were themselves eating into that capacity: in the seventh year of Daye, when the Sui mustered for the first campaign against Goguryeo, it called up 1.13 million men, nominally two million, drove its supplies as far as Liaodong and lost soldiers to the number of hundreds of thousands, and it campaigned against Goguryeo three more times in the eighth, ninth and eleventh years of Daye. In the same years drought and flood ruined the harvests of the Jianghuai and Jiangnan regions, the granaries could not be refilled, and runaway households and displaced peasants became the most direct source of manpower for the risings. For this campaign itself the only figures the sources give are the phrase that their numbers reached tens of thousands and the sequence that the prefectures and counties fell in turn; the actual strength of the rebels and of the government troops cannot be reconstructed. The rising broke out in the winter of the twelfth year of Daye and was settled by the beginning of the thirteenth, so the whole business lasted no more than two or three months, far shorter than the meaning it carried inside the collapsing order of the late Sui.
cause: 孫華起義的直接起因，是隋朝在大業年間把兵役、徭役與轉運同時壓在淮北沿線的鄉里身上。自大業六年起，隋煬帝兩度大舉征高句麗，又三次巡幸江都，每次出行都從沿運河、沿淮河的州縣抽丁、徵車、備糧；開皇十年所定的租調力役之制雖許人納絹代役，仍抵銷不了臨時加派與和雇之實。戰前一年的江南、江北大饑，又使大量農戶離鄉，成為流民與逃戶。大業十年，隋廷為整頓戶籍、追索亡戶而大索戶口，州郡胥吏乘機盤剝，鄉里對官府的怨望加深。孫華身為郡兵裨將，駐在蕭縣這個汴水沿線的交通節點上，平日所見即是徵發、催賦、督役與鄰里流亡；當流民成群地聚在市集渡口，而郡兵中又有同鄉的逃卒與被裁的鄉兵可以號召時，起義便以聚眾於鄉的形式爆發。這類起義不需要外部勢力策應，也不待號召，關鍵在於基層軍人與饑民在同一地點同時出現。
causeEn: The immediate occasion of Sun Hua's rising was that in the Daye era the Sui pressed service levies, forced labour and transport simultaneously onto the villages along the Huai and the canal. From the sixth year of Daye Emperor Yang launched two great campaigns against Goguryeo and made three further tours of Jiangdu, and each of these journeys drew men, carts and grain from the prefectures along the waterways; the rent-and-labour system fixed in the tenth year of Kaihuang, which allowed men to buy exemption from service with silk, could not offset the emergency levies and the requisition of carts actually made. A famine in the Jiangnan and Jianghuai regions in the year before the rising drove a further great number of households off their land, and they became the displaced and the runaway. In the tenth year of Daye the court made a general census of households to track down those who had fled, and the clerks of the prefectures and counties took the opportunity to squeeze the population harder, deepening the resentment of the villages against their own government. Sun Hua was a bingjiang of the commandery militia, posted at Xiao county, a traffic node on the Bian waterway, where he saw every day the levying of men, the pressing of taxes, the driving of labour and the flight of his neighbours; when displaced people gathered in numbers at the markets and crossings, and when among the local soldiers there were deserters and dismissed men of his own home district who could be called on, the revolt took the form of an armed mass rising in the villages. A rising of this kind needs no outside sponsor and no summons: what matters is that a soldier of the rank and file and hungry villagers are present in the same place at the same time.
impact: 此役的結果看似平淡，起義被平，首領被誅，州縣復歸朝廷，但它在隋末的局勢裡有三層作用。第一，它延續了隋朝對淮南漕運與州縣的直接控制：蕭縣一帶是汴水東段與泗州治所淤水之間的節點，叛軍曾經據此，說明帝國的內部秩序在名義上仍可維持，這使隋煬帝得以在平亂之後繼續他的巡幸安排，直到大業十三年的江都之變。第二，它暴露了隋代地方兵制的空殼：郡兵人數有限、訓練不足，遇數萬眾聚於一縣便需鄰州馳援，兵糧輸送線一旦被騷擾，平叛成本立刻上升；此後隋廷不得不倚重禁軍與新募的郡縣武人，地方武人因而逐步掌握兵柄，這正是隋亡之後群雄割據的制度前提。第三，它為接踵而至的起義浪潮提供了活的路標，大業七年王薄、大業九年楊玄感、大業十一年張金吾，到大業十三年的竇建德、杜伏威與瓦崗寨，叛軍首領與流民的路線一次又一次重疊在同一條江淮、淮北的交通線上，隋末的亂局因此由零星滋事變為席捲數州的崩解。
impactEn: The outcome looks undramatic, the rising suppressed, the leaders executed, the prefectures and counties returned to the government, yet it had three layers of consequence in the situation of the late Sui. First, it prolonged the Sui's direct control of the Huai river grain route and of the prefectures and counties: the area of Xiao was a node between the eastern stretch of the Bian waterway and Yushui, the seat of Si prefecture, and the rebels did hold it for a time, which shows that the internal order of the empire could still be maintained in form, and allowed Emperor Yang to continue his tours after the suppression, up to the change of power at Jiangdu in the thirteenth year of Daye. Second, it exposed the hollow shell of the Sui local military system: the commandery militia was few in number and poorly trained, and when tens of thousands gathered at a single county the neighbouring prefectures had to rush to its aid; once the line of supply was disturbed, the cost of the pacification rose at once. From then on the court had to lean on the palace guards and on newly raised commandery and county fighters, and local men with weapons gradually took the military power into their own hands, a precondition of the warlord fragmentation that followed the fall of the Sui. Third, it gave the wave of risings that followed a living example: the rebel leaders and the displaced travelled the same routes along the Jianghuai and the northern Huai again and again, from Wang Bo in the seventh year of Daye, Yang Xuangan in the ninth and Zhang Jinwu in the eleventh, to Dou Jiande, Du Fuwei and the Wagang stronghold in the thirteenth, so the disorder of the late Sui changed from scattered trouble into a collapse that swept several provinces.
result: 起義最終失敗。《隋書》與《資治通鑑》都記孫華部眾在起事後不久即被官軍擊破，首領孫華等人伏誅，餘眾散歸鄉里，泗州蕭縣等被攻陷的郡縣重新收復，隋廷照舊派遣郡兵與州兵駐守，並未因此改變州郡建置或兵制。從軍事上看，官軍的勝利有其結構性原因：叛軍雖眾至數萬，卻是臨時聚合的鄉里武裝，攻城靠內應，守城靠土築的城垣與坊里分隔，既無大型攻城器械，也無法從事長距離的補給；相較之下，隋朝仍握有京畿宿衛、州郡倉庫與漕運系統，可以承受短期內的調兵與運糧，這正是隋末早期民變多以失敗告終的關鍵。此役之後，隋朝表面的秩序得以維持約一年有餘，但造成起義的條件一項未改：徭役未減、兵役未停、倉廩未實、江北江南的饑荒未解。真正令隋朝崩解的並非這次被平息的叛亂，而是大業十三年（617年）起在河北、山東與中原腹地同時爆發的更大規模起義，以及大業十四年（618年）江都的政變。
resultEn: The rising failed in the end. Both the Suishu and the Zizhi Tongjian record that Sun Hua's mass was broken by government troops shortly after the outbreak, that the leaders including Sun Hua were executed, that the remainder scattered home, that the prefectures and counties that had fallen, Xiao county of Si prefecture among them, were recovered, and that the court went on stationing commandery and prefecture troops there without changing the administrative or military arrangements in response. Militarily the government victory had a structural reason: although the rebels numbered tens of thousands, they were a temporary mass of village fighters who took cities by insiders and defended themselves behind earthen ramparts and the lanes of the ward, and who had neither heavy siege equipment nor a means of supply over distance; the Sui, by contrast, still held the palace guards of the capital, the granaries of the prefectures and the canal system, and could bear the short-term cost of moving men and grain. That is the key to why the early popular risings of the late Sui so often ended in failure. After this campaign the outward order of the dynasty lasted a little over a year more, but not one of the conditions that produced the rising was changed: the levies were not reduced, the campaigns not halted, the granaries not filled, and the famine in the north and south of the river not relieved. What finally broke the Sui was not this suppressed revolt but the much larger risings that broke out at the same time in Hebei, Shandong and the central plains from the thirteenth year of Daye (617), and the coup at Jiangdu in the fourteenth year of Daye (618).
